claim: The Legislature meets every year in regular session
quote: The legislature shall meet annually in regular session for a limited number of legislative days

claim: Odd-year regular sessions convene at noon on the second Monday in April
quote: All regular sessions convening in odd-numbered years shall convene at noon on the second Monday in April

claim: Odd-year sessions last no more than 45 legislative days and end by the 60th calendar day
quote: shall continue beyond six o'clock in the evening of the sixtieth calendar day after convening

claim: Odd-year sessions are limited to fiscal matters, plus up to five prefiled non-fiscal bills per member and advertised local or special laws
quote: provided that the member shall not prefile more than five such matters pursuant to this Subsubparagraph

claim: Even-year regular sessions are general and convene at noon on the second Monday in March
quote: All regular sessions convening in even-numbered years shall be general in nature and shall convene at noon on the second Monday in March

claim: The governor may call an extraordinary session
quote: The legislature may be convened at other times by the governor

claim: A bill becomes law if the governor does not act within ten days of delivery during the session, or twenty days if the tenth day falls after adjournment
quote: or within twenty days after delivery if the tenth day after delivery occurs after the legislative session in which the bill passed is adjourned

claim: Laws from a regular session take effect on 1 August unless the bill sets another date
quote: All laws enacted during a regular session of the legislature shall take effect on August first of the calendar year in which the regular session is held

claim: A bill may set an earlier or later effective date
quote: However, any bill may specify an earlier or later effective date

claim: Political subdivisions may not adopt their own laws on elections unless the Election Code specifically authorizes it
quote: political subdivisions shall be prohibited from adopting any law, resolution, or ordinance relative to elections and the conduct thereof

claim: In the primary for every office except a party primary office, all voters vote regardless of party and all candidates run regardless of party
quote: Except for the election of persons to a party primary office in a party primary election, all qualified voters of this state may vote on candidates for public office in primary elections without regard to the voter's party affiliation

claim: General elections are open to all voters and candidates regardless of party
quote: All qualified voters of this state may vote on candidates for public office in general elections without regard to the voter's party affiliation

claim: Party primary offices are U.S. Senate and House, the state Supreme Court, BESE and the Public Service Commission
quote: "Party primary office" means an office of senator or representative in the United States Congress, justice of the supreme court, the State Board of Elementary and Secondary Education, and the Public Service Commission

claim: Party primaries are held on the spring election dates
quote: Party primary elections shall be held in an election year on the spring election dates established in R.S. 18:402

claim: In a party primary a voter may vote only for candidates of the voter's own party
quote: each voter voting in such election may vote only for a candidate who is affiliated with the same party as the voter

claim: Unaffiliated voters may choose one major party's primary ballot, and cannot switch party for the second party primary
quote: Voters not affiliated with a political party may vote in a major party primary if a party primary ballot is selected by the voter prior to casting his ballot

claim: Only candidates affiliated with a major party take part in that party's primary
quote: Only candidates affiliated with a major political party may participate in the party primary election of the political party of the candidate's party affiliation

claim: A party primary needs a majority; otherwise the top two of each party go to a second party primary
quote: the two candidates from each political party who received the greatest number of votes in the first party primary shall be voted on in the second party primary

claim: Candidates for party primary offices not affiliated with a major party go straight to the general election by petition
quote: who is not registered as being affiliated with a major political party shall file his notice of candidacy, which shall be accompanied by a nominating petition

claim: Only voters not affiliated with a major party may sign such a petition
quote: and who are not affiliated with a major political party

claim: In gubernatorial election years, the spring primary for municipal and ward officers is the third Saturday in April
quote: There shall be a spring primary election held on the third Saturday in April for municipal and ward officers elected in the spring of a gubernatorial election year

claim: The spring general election is the sixth Saturday after the spring primary
quote: There shall be a spring election held on the sixth Saturday after the third Saturday in April which shall be a general election for municipal and ward officers

claim: The fall gubernatorial primary is the third to last Saturday in October, for the governor and officers elected with the governor
quote: There shall be a fall primary election held on the third to last Saturday in October of a gubernatorial election year for governor and officers elected at the same time as the governor

claim: The fall gubernatorial general election is six Saturdays later
quote: There shall be a fall general election held on the sixth Saturday after the third to last Saturday in October of a gubernatorial election year

claim: In presidential years the spring municipal primary is the last Saturday in March
quote: there shall be a spring primary election held on the last Saturday in March for municipal and ward officers

claim: In congressional years the fall primary is the November federal election day
quote: There shall be a fall primary election held on the first Tuesday after the first Monday in November for officers elected at the same time as members of congress in that year

claim: In congressional years the fall general election is the sixth Saturday after the November primary
quote: There shall be a fall general election held on the sixth Saturday after the first Tuesday after the first Monday in November of a congressional election year

claim: Odd years without a governor's race also have spring municipal and ward elections
quote: There shall be a spring primary election held on the third Saturday in April for municipal and ward officers elected in the spring of a nongubernatorial election year

claim: In odd years without a governor's race, a parish containing a municipality of 300,000 or more holds a fall primary for parochial and municipal officers on the second Saturday in October
quote: There shall be a fall primary election held on the second Saturday in October for parochial and municipal officers in a parish containing a municipality with a population of three hundred thousand or more

claim: A candidate with a majority in the primary is elected
quote: A candidate who receives a majority of the votes cast for an office in a primary election is elected

claim: Unopposed candidates are declared elected and do not appear on the ballot
quote: the candidates for that office, or those remaining after the withdrawal of one or more candidates, are declared elected by the people

claim: Otherwise the top two (twice the number of seats) advance to the general election, whatever their party
quote: the candidates who qualify for each office remaining to be filled in the general election are those who received the two highest numbers of votes

claim: The general election field is twice the number of seats left to fill
quote: the number of candidates for an office who may qualify for the general election is twice the number of persons remaining to be elected to the office

claim: Every candidate's party, or "other" or "no party", is printed next to their name on primary and general ballots
quote: shall be listed on the primary or general election ballot on the same line and immediately after or below the candidate's name

claim: A candidate with no party affiliation is shown as "no party"
quote: If a candidate is not affiliated with any political party, the words "no party" or an abbreviation thereof shall be placed after his name

claim: The ballot order lists local offices including police juror, school board member and justice of the peace, and municipal offices including mayor, chief of police and alderman
quote: Municipal offices--mayor, chief of police or marshal, alderman or member of a city council

claim: A candidate lists their registered party, "other" or "no party" on the notice of candidacy
quote: or "no party" or an abbreviation thereof if he is registered with no political party affiliation

claim: No party may be recognized under the name "Independent"
quote: no political party shall be recognized in this state which declares its name solely to be "Independent" or the "Independent Party"

claim: A candidate qualifies by filing a notice of candidacy with either a nominating petition or the qualifying fee
quote: shall qualify as a candidate by timely filing notice of his candidacy, which shall be accompanied either by a nominating petition or by the qualifying fee

claim: Petition signers must be registered to vote on the office the candidate seeks, and may not withdraw a signature
quote: Once a voter has signed a nominating petition, he may not withdraw the nomination

claim: Petition signers must be registered to vote on the office
quote: registered to vote on the office he seeks who sign a nominating petition for him

claim: A person under an order of imprisonment for a felony conviction cannot qualify
quote: shall qualify to become a candidate if he is under an order of imprisonment for conviction of a felony

claim: Parish school board members are elected at the congressional elections for four-year concurrent terms beginning 1 January
quote: members of parish school boards shall be elected at the congressional elections

claim: School board terms are four-year concurrent terms beginning January 1
quote: Members elected in 1986 and thereafter shall serve four-year concurrent terms beginning January 1 following their election

claim: A school board could move its elections to the fall gubernatorial election by a plan, starting in 2031
quote: The first election under the plan shall be held at the 2031 fall gubernatorial election

claim: The legislature creates parish school boards and provides for the election of their members
quote: The legislature shall create parish school boards and provide for the election of their members

claim: Existing parish and city school systems are recognized
quote: Parish and city school board systems in existence on the effective date of this constitution are recognized

claim: Monroe City and Ouachita Parish school boards have separate electorates
quote: Only persons residing within the jurisdiction of the Monroe City School Board shall be eligible to vote for or be members of the Monroe City School Board

claim: A charter cannot change a school board inconsistently with the constitution or law
quote: No home rule charter or plan of government shall contain any provision affecting a school board

claim: East Baton Rouge Parish School Board has its own membership law
quote: East Baton Rouge Parish School Board shall continue to consist of twelve members elected at the congressional elections

claim: Justices of the peace are elected at the congressional election for six-year terms
quote: Justices of the peace shall be elected at the congressional election for terms of six years

claim: Constables are elected at the congressional election for six-year terms, one for each justice of the peace court
quote: A constable shall be elected at the congressional election for terms of six years

claim: City court marshals or constables are elected at the congressional election for six-year terms, except Baton Rouge's city constable
quote: each marshal or constable shall be elected at the congressional election

claim: Baton Rouge's city constable is elected under the city charter and the parish plan of government
quote: The city constable of the city of Baton Rouge shall be elected in accordance with and pursuant to the applicable provisions of the charter of the city of Baton Rouge

claim: Mayors' courts and justice of the peace courts are continued by the constitution
quote: Mayors' courts and justice of the peace courts existing on the effective date of this constitution are continued

claim: Parishes and their boundaries are recognized by the constitution
quote: Parishes and their boundaries as established on the effective date of this constitution are recognized and ratified

claim: A police jury sets its own size by ordinance, between 5 and 15 members (3 in parishes of 10,000 or fewer)
quote: no police jury shall have less than five members nor more than fifteen members

claim: Small parishes may have as few as three police jurors
quote: parishes with a population of ten thousand persons or less may establish the size of the body at not less than three members

claim: Police jurors are elected at the state general election for four-year terms
quote: Police jurors shall be elected at the state general election and shall serve for terms of four years

claim: Police jurors take office on the second Monday in January after their election and elect a president from among themselves
quote: the police jury shall elect a president from their own number

claim: A police jury may divide the parish into up to twelve police jury wards
quote: may redistrict their parish into not more than twelve police jury wards

claim: Each parish elects a sheriff for four years, except Orleans Parish where this section does not apply
quote: In each parish a sheriff shall be elected for a term of four years

claim: The constitutional sheriff section does not apply to Orleans Parish
quote: This Section shall not apply to Orleans Parish

claim: Each parish elects a clerk of the district court for four years
quote: In each parish a clerk of the district court shall be elected for a term of four years

claim: Each parish elects a coroner for four years
quote: In each parish a coroner shall be elected for a term of four years

claim: Each parish elects a tax assessor for four years
quote: A tax assessor shall be elected by the electors of each parish. His term of office shall be four years

claim: Orleans Parish's assessor is elected with New Orleans's municipal officers
quote: The assessor shall be elected at the same time as the municipal officers of New Orleans

claim: A charter cannot change the offices of district attorney, sheriff, assessor, clerk of court or coroner inconsistently with the constitution or law
quote: or the offices of district attorney, sheriff, assessor, clerk of a district court, or coroner, which is inconsistent with this constitution or law

claim: Any parish or municipality may adopt a home rule charter; there is no population threshold
quote: any local governmental subdivision may draft, adopt, or amend a home rule charter in accordance with this Section

claim: "Local governmental subdivision" means a parish or municipality
quote: "Local governmental subdivision" means any parish or municipality

claim: A municipality means an incorporated city, town or village
quote: "Municipality" means an incorporated city, town, or village

claim: A charter is adopted by majority vote of the electors
quote: A home rule charter shall be adopted, amended, or repealed when approved by a majority of the electors voting thereon

claim: A charter sets the structure and organization of the local government
quote: A home rule charter adopted under this Section shall provide the structure and organization, powers, and functions of the government

claim: Two or more subdivisions in one parish may adopt a joint charter
quote: Two or more local governmental subdivisions within the boundaries of one parish may adopt a home rule charter under this Section

claim: Charters and plans of government existing in 1974 remain in effect
quote: Every home rule charter or plan of government existing or adopted when this constitution is adopted shall remain in effect

claim: The legislature may not change the structure of a home rule charter government
quote: The legislature shall enact no law the effect of which changes or affects the structure and organization

claim: The legislature may classify parishes and municipalities by population
quote: The legislature may classify parishes or municipalities according to population or on any other reasonable basis

claim: Municipal incorporation and government are set by general law; local laws cannot create a municipality or amend a municipal charter, except pre-1974 special legislative charters
quote: No local or special law shall create a municipal corporation or amend, modify, or repeal a municipal charter

claim: Municipalities are cities (5,000 or more), towns (1,001 to 4,999) and villages (1,000 or fewer)
quote: Those having five thousand inhabitants or more are cities; those having less than five thousand but more than one thousand inhabitants are towns; and those having one thousand or fewer inhabitants are villages

claim: A change of class needs a resolution and a governor's proclamation; a census alone does not change it
quote: If the governor finds that the municipality is wrongly classified, he shall issue a proclamation correctly classifying the municipality

claim: A village that grows by fewer than 200 people into town size may choose to stay a village
quote: the governing authority of a municipality may elect not to change the classification of the municipality

claim: Lawrason Act municipalities may call their board a village, town or city council and its members council members
quote: elect to be known and referred to as a village, town, or city council

claim: The Lawrason Act (mayor and board of aldermen) governs every municipality without a special legislative charter or home rule charter
quote: All municipalities shall be governed by the provisions of this Part except those municipalities governed by a special legislative charter or a home rule charter

claim: A special legislative charter governs where it speaks; the Lawrason Act fills gaps
quote: if the provisions of the special legislative charter are silent on a particular matter, then the provisions of Part I of Chapter 2

claim: Lawrason municipal officers are a mayor, aldermen, a chief of police, a tax collector and a clerk
quote: The officers of every municipality shall be a mayor, aldermen, a chief of police, a tax collector, and a clerk

claim: The mayor and chief of police are elected at large
quote: The mayor and chief of police in all municipalities shall be elected at large

claim: Some municipalities appoint their chief of police, under pre-1970 practice or special laws
quote: Municipalities where the chief of police is appointed rather than elected as of

claim: In some municipalities the elected chief of police is called the marshal
quote: The marshal who is the chief of police in such municipalities shall be elected at large

claim: In municipalities of 5,000 or less, voters may choose to have an appointed or elected marshal
quote: authorize the mayor to thereafter appoint a marshal who is the chief of police with the approval of the governing authority or provide for the election of a marshal

claim: Cities have 5 to 9 aldermen, towns 5 and villages 3
quote: The number of aldermen in a city shall be not less than five nor more than nine; the number of aldermen in a town shall be five; and the number of aldermen in a village shall be three

claim: Village aldermen are elected at large
quote: Aldermen in villages shall be elected at large

claim: Lawrason municipal officers serve four-year terms
quote: municipal elections shall be held every four years

claim: Lawrason officers take office on 1 July and serve four years
quote: The officers elected shall take office on the first day of July following their election and shall hold their office for four years

claim: A municipality may, by irrevocable plan, move its elections to the congressional elections
quote: Any municipality by ordinance of the governing authority may adopt a plan for holding municipal elections at the congressional elections

claim: Such a plan cannot be revoked
quote: No such plan shall be revocable by the governing authority

claim: A municipality may file a plan to move to the fall gubernatorial election, first used in 2031
quote: Any plan adopted pursuant to this Paragraph shall be filed with the secretary of state no later than January 12, 2027

claim: The first fall gubernatorial municipal election under such a plan is 2031
quote: The first election under the plan shall be held at the 2031 gubernatorial election

claim: Charter commissions may be appointed or elected for any parish or municipality
quote: Any parish or municipality may draft, adopt, or amend a home rule charter

claim: Officers of a newly incorporated municipality are appointed by the governor until the next municipal election
quote: The governor shall appoint all the officers of a newly incorporated municipality

claim: For Orleans Parish, the parish governing authority is the city council
quote: "Parish governing authority" or "governing authority of the parish" with respect to Orleans Parish means the city council

claim: Lafayette's unified city-parish plan remains in effect as a local and special act
quote: dealing with the charter commission and the plan for unification of the parish and city of Lafayette

claim: Terrebonne Parish's plan of government remains in effect as a local and special act
quote: dealing with the charter commission and plan of government for Terrebonne Parish

claim: Baton Rouge and East Baton Rouge Parish share a plan of government
quote: the applicable provisions of the plan of government for the parish of East Baton Rouge and the city of Baton Rouge

claim: Where a municipality has over half of a parish's people, it gets proportionate representation on the parish school board
quote: the municipality shall have representation on the parish school board proportionate to its population
